inline_comments.comment:
The captured group `match[1]` from `^gitdir:\s+(.+)$` retains any trailing whitespace that appears before end-of-line (e.g. a trailing space or carriage return on CRLF files). The `gitPointer.trim()` call only strips the outer file content, not the captured value. Passing a path with trailing whitespace to `resolvePath` would silently produce a wrong path. Consider trimming the captured group:
```ts
return resolvePath(repoRoot, match[1].trim());
```

The `gitDiffProvider` option type was changed from `Pick<GitDiffProvider, 'getChangedFiles' | 'getRepoRoot'>` to the concrete `GitDiffProvider` class. This makes the API less flexible: callers can no longer pass a plain object that structurally satisfies the interface; they must extend the class. Although tests work around this via the new `MockGitDiffProvider` subclass, the loss of structural typing is a breaking change for any external consumer that builds a custom provider. If multi-subscriber support (`onGitStateChange`) is what necessitated moving to the full class, consider extracting a `GitDiffProviderInterface` (or simply re-exporting the expanded `Pick`) so the contract remains structural.

`FSWatcher` (line 1) and `watch` (line 3) are both imported from `'node:fs'` via two separate `import type` statements. These can be consolidated into one:
```ts
import type { FSWatcher, watch } from 'node:fs';
```
This also removes the need for the intermediary `node:fs/promises` import line to be sandwiched between them.

`void callback;` is an unusual idiom to suppress an "unused variable" warning. Readers unfamiliar with this pattern may mistake it for an intentional side-effect. The conventional TypeScript approach is to prefix the parameter with an underscore (`_callback`) to signal it is intentionally unused, which most linters and readers recognise without needing an explicit `void` expression.

general_comments.comment: The generation-counter approach (incrementing `watcherSetupGeneration` on every unsubscribe to invalidate in-flight setup) is a solid pattern for cancellable async workflows, but it means the counter is monotonically increasing and shared across all subscriber sessions. A comment explaining _why_ a generation number is used (rather than a simple boolean `cancelled` flag) would help future maintainers understand the design intent, especially since the watcher lifecycle spans several async methods (`ensureWatchers`, `setupWatchers`, `watchFile`, `configureBranchWatcher`) that all thread the generation through as a parameter.

The `MockGitDiffProvider` class pattern introduced in the tests is cleaner than the previous plain-object mocks, but each test that needs specific mock behavior must call `createMockGitDiffProvider` with a configure callback. Tests that only need default behaviour (empty sets, no-op watchers) use `createMockGitDiffProvider()` with no argument, which is readable. However, the returned `MockGitDiffProvider` instance exposes `getChangedFilesMock`, `getRepoRootMock`, and `onGitStateChangeMock` as public readonly fields; any code with access to the instance can mutate the mock. Marking these as `readonly` is already done, but the naming convention (`*Mock` suffix) and direct access pattern differs from the rest of the test suite's `vi.fn()` usage — a brief comment explaining the pattern would help new contributors follow it.
